newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Moisture good for Ukraine grain conditions - expert.
newsitem.headline: Moisture good for Ukraine grain conditions - expert.

text.p: Ukraine's winter wheat crop prospects look good due to higher-than-average soil moisture in grain-producing areas which will provide protection against any summer drought, an agriculture expert said on Thursday.

"Nice quantities of moisture in most areas of Ukraine are creating good conditions for winter wheat, and lead us to expect a good harvest," Volodymyr Krut, deputy head of the Ukrainian Academy of Agrarian Sciences, told Reuters.

"The biggest problem has been dryness in the steppes of central and southern Ukraine, but moisture there is 1.5 times higher than average," he said. "If we had a drought that moisture would protect our wheat."
Krut said winter wheat was growing well in Ukraine, which has forecast a harvest of 20.8 million tonnes compared to 13.4 million harvested last year.
Officials have forecast a total grain crop of 35 million tonnes this year against last year's poor 25.4 million tonne harvest following drought at the start of the growing season.
Krut said the moisture would also compensate for temperatures which were one to two degrees lower than average this month and last.

The cooler weather had delayed sowing of early spring grains like barley and oats, and also sugarbeet, he said but added, "We expect warm, sunny weather will finally arrive to stay in the next few days and allow our sowing schedule to return to normal."
He added that early weather forecasts indicated dry conditions like last year's would not return this year.
The Statistics Ministry said 4.0 million hectares have been sown with spring grain against 1.6 million hectares sown by this time last year when the weather was even colder than now.
The ministry also said Ukraine has sown 263,000 hectares to sugarbeet against 9,000 ha at this time in 1996. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 244-9150
